card.name: Inside hyphenated headings and compounds
card.fires_on: The word just before a hyphen in a hyphenated title or compound, such as the 'us' in Graft-Versus-Host or 'to' in Moderate-to-Severe. It also fires on 'ia' in Ischemia in section headings.

modes.label: Versus in Graft-Versus-Host
modes.description: The 'us' ending of Versus inside the disease name Graft-Versus-Host Disease.

modes.label: Hyphenated phrase parts
modes.description: The first or middle piece of a hyphen chain such as Moderate-to-Severe, Week-by-Week or Self-Sufficient.
modes.example: with Moderate<<-to>>-Severe Plaque Psoriasis Body Weight

modes.label: Ischemia heading
modes.description: The 'ia' ending of Ischemia in the numbered warning heading Myocardial Ischemia.

card.writes: It suppresses odd continuations and promotes capitalized sentence-starting words, so it seems to prepare for a new heading or sentence to begin.
card.plain: It fires in the middle of a hyphenated heading or compound, where the phrase is not yet finished.
